commands.pkgnames.txt: apt-cache pkgnames <the first two characters of the unknown name>

notes: The stock Ubuntu 24.04 cloud image already carries bc, ed, patch, jq and time, so the declared names are tree, sqlite3 and a per-distro zip, with whois as the hand-installed control; all of those are absent from both stock images.
The interrupted scenario was recorded on Debian 12 only: both of its names are absent from that stock image, and one real kill produces all three classifications.

The dpkg-query command above is the one that really produced these bytes on those guests in 2026-09, and is not edited: M-Import R-1 (LD-312) later changed the product's format string from ${binary:Package} to ${Package}, so a recording taken today would carry plain names where these carry architecture-qualified ones. Nothing this suite concludes depends on which spelling the recording uses -- the apply compares declared names against the recording it is given -- and re-recording would need a guest, which R-1 did not create.

states.before: the machine before the apply under test
states.dirty: a package unpacked and not configured, which is what dpkg --audit really prints
states.partial: one of the interrupted transaction's two packages installed and the other not, which is neither bracket

what: Every file under this directory is the verbatim standard output of one command on one fresh disposable guest of this task, fetched off that guest by docs/milestones/m-0.6/probes/hostvm.py --record-fixtures. Nothing here is written by hand or invented: tests/host_apt.rs replays these bytes through shims it owns, so an assertion about what lodi concludes is an assertion about what apt really said.
